name: bitblocks-interop-vectors
description: Test vectors for payments that carry their own proof: BEEF V1 (BRC-62), BEEF V2 (BRC-96), Atomic BEEF (BRC-95) and BUMP (BRC-74). Each states what it should do, with where it came from.
versioning: Within v1, a vector's id, bytes and expected outcome stay as they are, except to correct a mistake, which the version number and this file will show. New vectors raise the minor version. A change to what outcomes mean gets a new file.
claim: These vectors cover inclusion in a block. They say whether a transaction's bytes sit under a merkle root in a header. They don't say a transaction is valid, its scripts pass, its inputs were unspent, a token is genuine or a payment was made.
licence_notice: © BSV Association. Vectors from BRCs and @bsv/sdk fall under the Open BSV License, full text at the licence URL. Each source below says which applies.
tried_against: One SDK, @bsv/sdk 2.4.0, in a one-off run, and no live wallet. Nothing in this file says any wallet, SDK or project conforms to it or endorses it.
how_to_use: Treat the entries in headers_held as the headers you hold, and no others. Each one is looked up in headers by height.
For a beef vector, decode hex, read it, and compare your answer with expected.
For a bump vector, decode hex, read it as one BUMP with nothing left over, and climb each named txid to the root.
outcome is the result to match. reason is the name Bitblocks uses, so yours may differ.

fields.valid: true: a conforming sender could produce these bytes. false: deliberately wrong, or short of what a sender owes.
fields.basis: The BRC whose rule this vector exercises, or hardening: a stricter reading Bitblocks applies where a spec is silent or leaves room. A reader may differ on a hardening vector and still follow the spec.
fields.headers: synthetic: false is a real mainnet header, with its 80 bytes to check for yourself. synthetic: true is a root made up for this kit, for use in this kit only.
fields.tx_count: A block's transaction count. It isn't in the 80-byte header, so it comes from outside it.

outcomes.proven: Its bytes hash to its txid, its BUMP climbs to a root, and that root is the one in a header you rely on at that height.
outcomes.anchored: It has no BUMP, and every input leads, within this BEEF, to proven transactions. It is not itself shown to be in a block.
outcomes.unknown: The checker can't say: no header at that height, or the BEEF lacks what it needs. Never read this as a pass.
outcomes.failed: The evidence is wrong: the root differs from the header, the BUMP reaches no root or can't be that block's, or an ancestor failed.
outcomes.refused: The bytes can't be read as this format.
outcomes.root: A BUMP vector: each named txid climbs to this root at this offset.

vectors.title: BRC-62's example: a proven parent and a fresh payment
vectors.description: The spec's own example. The parent has a BUMP into block 814435, and the subject has none, so it is anchored and is not shown to be in a block.

vectors.title: The same bytes, with no header at that height
vectors.description: Good bytes and a checker that holds no header at 814435. The answer is unknown, never a pass.

vectors.title: BRC-62's example as Atomic BEEF
vectors.description: The SDK's Atomic BEEF around the BRC-62 transactions. BRC-95 doesn't say which byte order the subject takes; this vector has it in internal order, as the SDK writes it.

vectors.title: BEEF V2 with the parent as a txid alone
vectors.description: BRC-96 lets two parties who already share a transaction send its txid and treat it as valid. A third party has no such agreement, so a checker with no earlier exchange answers unknown.

vectors.title: Two inputs: one mined, one unconfirmed, BEEF V1
vectors.description: A test transaction spending a proven output and an unconfirmed one. Its merkle root is a test value, so hold the synthetic header at this height. Against real headers it reads failed.

vectors.title: The same transactions as BEEF V2
vectors.description: Rewritten by @bsv/sdk 2.4.0 from the BEEF V1 above. The same test merkle root applies.

vectors.title: The same transactions as Atomic BEEF
vectors.description: Rewritten by @bsv/sdk 2.4.0 from the BEEF V1 above. The same test merkle root applies.

vectors.title: A real mainnet transaction, BEEF V1
vectors.description: WhatsOnChain's transaction and BUMP, put together as BEEF V1 by Bitblocks. The subject has its own proof, against a real header.

vectors.title: The same transaction, BEEF V2
vectors.description: The same bytes in the V2 layout, put together by Bitblocks.

vectors.title: The same transaction, Atomic BEEF around V1
vectors.description: The Atomic prefix and subject around the V1 vector, subject in internal byte order.

vectors.title: The same transaction, Atomic BEEF around V2
vectors.description: The Atomic prefix and subject around the V2 vector, subject in internal byte order.

vectors.title: A chain of unconfirmed transactions from one proof
vectors.description: Crafted: a proven transaction, a child and a grandchild. Anchoring carries down the chain.

vectors.title: A block of one transaction
vectors.description: Crafted: the transaction is its block's merkle root, so its BUMP is one leaf at level 0.

vectors.title: BRC-74's example: three transactions, one path
vectors.description: The spec's own example. Each named txid climbs to the root in block 813706's header.

vectors.title: A real mainnet path
vectors.description: WhatsOnChain's BUMP for one transaction in block 973110.

vectors.title: No bytes at all
vectors.description: An empty input.

vectors.title: A version we can't read
vectors.description: 0300beef isn't a defined BEEF version.

vectors.title: Cut one byte short
vectors.description: mainnet-v1 without its last byte.

vectors.title: A byte past the end
vectors.description: mainnet-v1 with one more byte.

vectors.title: No transactions
vectors.description: No BUMPs and no transactions, so there is no subject.

vectors.title: A VarInt longer than it needs to be
vectors.description: mainnet-v1 with its BUMP count written as fd0100.

vectors.title: A transaction with no inputs
vectors.description: This also refuses Extended Format, whose marker reads as an input count of zero. BEEF carries raw transactions (BRC-12).

vectors.title: A has-BUMP flag other than 0 or 1
vectors.description: mainnet-v1 with the flag set to 02.

vectors.title: A BEEF V2 format byte outside 00, 01 and 02
vectors.description: One transaction entry with format 03.

vectors.title: A BUMP index past the list
vectors.description: mainnet-v1 pointing at a second BUMP it doesn't have.

vectors.title: The same transaction twice
vectors.description: mainnet-v1's transaction listed two times.

vectors.title: A child ahead of its parent
vectors.description: BRC-62's example with its two transactions swapped.

vectors.title: Atomic BEEF naming a transaction it doesn't hold
vectors.description: mainnet-v1 wrapped with BRC-62's payment as the subject.

vectors.title: Atomic BEEF holding a transaction outside the subject's ancestry
vectors.description: BRC-62's example wrapped with the parent as the subject, so the payment is unrelated.

vectors.title: A block height past 2^32 - 1
vectors.description: A height no block header can hold.

vectors.title: A tree height of 0
vectors.description: A BUMP with no levels proves nothing.

vectors.title: A tree height of 65
vectors.description: BRC-74 caps the tree height at 64.

vectors.title: No leaves at level 0
vectors.description: Nothing to climb from.

vectors.title: An offset that can't fit the tree
vectors.description: Offset 2 in a tree of height 1.

vectors.title: Two leaves at one offset
vectors.description: Both at offset 0.

vectors.title: A leaf flag outside 00, 01 and 02
vectors.description: Flag 03.

vectors.title: A duplicate flag at an even offset
vectors.description: A duplicate stands for the right-hand node of a last pair, so its offset is odd.

vectors.title: A proof pointed at the wrong block
vectors.description: BRC-62's BUMP with its height changed to 813706, whose real header has another root. The subject fails with its ancestor.

vectors.title: A changed hash in the path
vectors.description: BRC-62's example with one sibling at level 0 hashed again. The climb reaches some other root.

vectors.title: A changed transaction
vectors.description: BRC-62's parent with its last byte flipped, so it has another txid and isn't a leaf of the BUMP.

vectors.title: A path with a node missing
vectors.description: Crafted: three levels, and nothing at offset 1 of level 0 or above to climb with.

vectors.title: A tree height that doesn't fit the block
vectors.description: Crafted: the root matches, but a block of 1,000 transactions has a tree of height 10, and this BUMP has 1. That shape would let an inner node pose as a leaf.

vectors.title: An offset past the block's last transaction
vectors.description: Crafted: the root matches, but the block has one transaction and this one sits at offset 1.

vectors.title: A 64-byte transaction
vectors.description: Crafted: 64 bytes is also the preimage of an inner merkle node, so such a transaction could pose as a leaf.

vectors.title: A transaction whose parent isn't there
vectors.description: Crafted: no BUMP and no parent in the BEEF, so it leads to no proof. BRC-62 asks for the ancestors; a reader can still answer unknown.

vectors.title: A coinbase with no proof
vectors.description: Crafted: a coinbase has no parents to lead to, so without its own BUMP nothing supports it.
